root_cause.text: In XFS xattr leaf block insertion, `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work()` only adjusted the freemap entry at the old end of the leaf entry array, leaving later `freemap[]` entries uncorrected when the entries array grew and causing the freemap to overlap the leaf entry array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work()` to compute `old_end`/`new_end` and then, for every `freemap[i]`, shift any entry whose `base` equals `old_end` or whose free region starts before `new_end`; the commit message explains the bug where `freemap[0]` is moved up but `freemap[1]` “hasn't been updated, and now the entries array and the free space claim the same space,” triggering `ASSERT(ichdr->firstused >= ichdr->count * sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t) + xfs_attr3_leaf_hdr_size(leaf))`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add local variables needed for upcoming attribute leaf add logic.
intent_record.what: The function `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work()` adds two new local integer variables, `old_end` and `new_end`, alongside the existing variable declarations.
intent_record.how: This change only introduces storage for additional values that will be used later in the function; by itself it does not alter runtime behavior, but it enables subsequent logic to track old and new end positions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix freemap adjustment logic in xfs attribute leaf growth to correctly account for expanded leaf entry array space.
intent_record.what: The code replaces the old single-position freemap adjustment logic with new calculations for `new_end` and `old_end` using `struct xfs_attr_leaf_entry`, changes the assertion to check `firstused >= new_end`, and updates the freemap loop to adjust entries either when they start at the old array end or when they overlap the newly occupied space, using a computed `diff` and subtracting that amount from the freemap size.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the leaf free-space map is now updated more accurately when the attribute leaf entry array grows, preventing freemap entries from incorrectly pointing into space now occupied by the expanded array and preserving correct free-space accounting.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds local variables in preparation for later attribute leaf add logic and does not address the freemap adjustment bug or overlapping leaf/freemap issue described in the root cause.

The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes freemap adjustment during XFS xattr leaf entry growth so later freemap entries are updated correctly and do not overlap the expanded leaf entry array.

candidates.rationale: This computes only the old end of the leaf entry array, so the subsequent freemap adjustment was anchored to the previous boundary rather than the newly expanded array size. That matches the root cause where only the freemap entry at the old end was corrected, leaving later freemap entries overlapping the enlarged leaf entry array.

This condition limits adjustment to a single freemap entry whose base exactly matches the old array end. Because later freemap entries are not updated, growth of the leaf entry array can cause freemap regions to overlap the entry array.

vuln_statements.explanation: This computes the old end of the leaf entry array instead of the newly expanded boundary, so the later freemap correction is anchored to the wrong offset and can leave freemap entries overlapping the grown leaf entry array.
This restricts adjustment to only the freemap entry whose base exactly matches the old array end, leaving any later freemap entries uncorrected when the leaf entry array expands.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described is the failure to properly adjust freemap entries when the leaf entry array grows. In this function, that handling is present and explicit: after inserting the entry, it computes the old boundary with `tmp = (ichdr->count - 1) * sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t) + xfs_attr3_leaf_hdr_size(leaf);` and then iterates over all freemap slots: `for (i = 0; i < XFS_ATTR_LEAF_MAPSIZE; i++) { if (ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp) { ichdr->freemap[i].base += sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); ichdr->freemap[i].size -= sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); } }`. This shows the code already updates any freemap entry that starts at the old end of the entry array, preventing overlap. Therefore the buggy condition is absent here and the fix is already present.
